Article Title: Microsoft net income rises 32% to $36.6 billion days after buyout offer to 60,000 staff
Article Text:
Microsoft posts $36.6 billion profit as 60,000 staff offered voluntary exits

Microsoft Cloud revenue rises 30%, Azure grows 48%

Microsoft projects December-quarter revenue of up to $97.1 billion

Capital expenditure expected to exceed $50 billion in December quarter

Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to around 60,000 employees

Microsoft reported a 32 per cent year-on-year rise in net income to $36.6 billion in the July-September quarter, days after announcing a voluntary buyout offer for around 60,000 employees, more than a quarter of its global workforce.India is among the four countries where the offer applies, alongside the US, Canada and the UK.The technology major began fiscal year 2027 with higher revenue and earnings, supported by strong growth in its cloud business. Revenue for the first quarter ended September 30, 2026, rose 19 per cent to $92.3 billion from $77.7 billion in the corresponding quarter last year. Operating income increased 21 per cent to $45.9 billion.Microsoft's cloud business remained a key contributor to its results, with Microsoft Cloud revenue reaching $63.9 billion, up 30 per cent year-on-year and 31 per cent in constant currency. Azure revenue grew 48 per cent during the quarter.Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella highlighted the performance in a post on X. “Just wrapped our earnings call. It was a fast start to our fiscal year. Microsoft Cloud revenue surpassed $63B, with growth accelerating to 30% YoY,” he said.Revenue from Microsoft's Agents and Infra segment rose 25 per cent to $76.8 billion. The company's commercial remaining performance obligation, which represents contracted revenue yet to be recognised, increased 73 per cent to $677 billion.“We delivered a strong start to the fiscal year with Microsoft Cloud revenue of $63.9 billion, with growth accelerating to 30% (up 31% in constant currency) year-over-year,” said Amy Hood, Microsoft's executive vice president and chief financial officer. She added that the company exceeded expectations across revenue, operating income and earnings per share.Diluted earnings per share increased 32 per cent to $4.92 on a reported basis. Excluding the impact of investments in OpenAI, adjusted net income rose 18 per cent to $36.4 billion, while adjusted earnings per share increased 18 per cent to $4.89.Microsoft expects revenue of $96 billion to $97.1 billion in the December quarter, representing growth of 18-19 per cent. Azure revenue growth is projected at 49-50 per cent in constant currency.Hood said customer demand continues to exceed available supply, while improvements in the efficiency of the company's computing infrastructure are helping it serve more demand.Microsoft's capital expenditure stood at $45.2 billion in the September quarter. Hood expects spending to exceed $50 billion in the December quarter, with capital expenditure for calendar year 2026 projected at approximately $170 billion. The estimate partly reflects capacity deliveries delayed from earlier periods.However, not all business segments recorded growth. Revenue from Microsoft's Devices and Consumer segment declined 3 per cent to $15.5 billion. Windows OEM and devices revenue fell 22 per cent, while Xbox content and services revenue declined 2 per cent. Search and advertising revenue, excluding traffic acquisition costs, grew 12 per cent.The company's financial performance comes as it offers voluntary buyouts to around 60,000 employees, more than a quarter of its global workforce. Chief people officer Amy Coleman announced the Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO) in a memo to staff on Monday, presenting it as an option for employees already considering a future outside Microsoft to leave with financial support and career planning assistance.The terms mirror Microsoft's standard severance arrangements. Eligible employees in the US, Canada, the UK and India at level 70 and below have until the first week of December to decide whether to accept the offer. The level band extends up to general managers and some vice presidents. Employees who accept will leave the company at the end of the year.Unlike the retirement buyout Microsoft offered earlier this year, the VEO has no age or tenure requirement, and performance does not determine eligibility.However, the offer is not available to every employee at level 70 or below. Microsoft has left the decision on participation to individual business leaders. Coleman's memo said participation would depend on each unit's priorities, customer commitments and workforce needs.
Article Summary: Microsoft posts $36.6 billion profit as 60,000 staff offered voluntary exits. Cloud revenue rises 30%, Azure grows 48% in July-September quarter. Microsoft projects December-quarter revenue of up to $97.1 billion.Capital expenditure expected to exceed $50 billion in December quarter.

Article Title: Amazon shares sink 7% as AI spending fuels cash-burn concerns, overshadow cloud growth
Article Text:
Amazon cloud business accelerates but shares drop on profit miss

Cash burn and outlook weigh on sentiment

Advertising business misses expectations

AI spending pressures spread across Big Tech

Amazon shares fell sharply in after-hours trading on Thursday (local time) as heavy artificial intelligence investments and a weaker-than-expected earnings performance overshadowed accelerating growth in its cloud computing business.The e-commerce and technology giant’s shares dropped as much as 7% after it reported third-quarter results that missed Wall Street expectations and issued a cautious revenue outlook for the crucial holiday shopping quarter. The stock had already fallen 4.3% during regular trading to close at $243.79.Amazon’s cloud computing unit, Amazon Web Services (AWS), delivered a standout performance, with revenue rising 39% year-on-year to $46 billion in the quarter ended September 30. This marked its fastest growth in nearly five years and accelerated from the 37% increase recorded in the previous quarter. Revenue also exceeded analysts’ expectations of $45.61 billion, according to LSEG data.However, investors remained concerned about the cost of expanding the business to capitalise on growing demand for artificial intelligence. Amazon has forecast capital expenditure of $220 billion for 2026, largely to build AI data centres and expand its technology infrastructure.Chief executive Andy Jassy told analysts that capital expenditure would be “meaningfully more” next year, without providing a specific figure. “Our strategy is working and I expect it will for the foreseeable future,” Jassy said, defending the company’s investment plans.He also said AWS could become a business generating more than $1 trillion in annual revenue within five to 10 years, adding that demand for the unit’s services remained strong.“Customers are gobbling it up,” Jassy said, referring to the rapid adoption of Amazon’s AI infrastructure.Amazon’s spending plans have raised questions about how quickly its AI investments will translate into stronger cash generation. The company reported a trailing 12-month cash burn of $42.4 billion in the September quarter, driven by heavy capital expenditure. Spending on capital projects during the quarter reached $77.26 billion, around $20 billion above estimates compiled by LSEG.“The free cash flow looks like the ugly part of the report,” said Dave Wagner, portfolio manager at Aptus Capital Advisors. “Operations generated plenty of cash but their capex just absolutely swallowed it.”Amazon reported net sales of $201.94 billion for the quarter, up 12% from $180.17 billion a year earlier. Net income declined to $20.69 billion, or $1.89 per share, from $21.19 billion, or $1.95 per share, in the year-ago period. Analysts had expected earnings of $1.97 per share on revenue of $202.2 billion, according to FactSet.The company forecast fourth-quarter net sales of between $240 billion and $247 billion, representing growth of 12% to 16% from a year earlier. The midpoint of the range, $243.5 billion, was slightly below analysts’ estimate of $244.51 billion, according to LSEG.The outlook covers the holiday shopping season, a crucial period for Amazon’s retail business, as consumers contend with elevated living costs and higher fuel prices.Amazon’s advertising division also disappointed investors. Revenue rose 12 per cent to $19.6 billion, falling short of analysts’ expectations for growth of 18%. It was the first time in seven quarters that the business missed estimates, according to Reuters.The slowdown contrasted with growth of 26% in the previous quarter and 22% in the year-ago period. Jassy attributed some of the weakness to the timing of the company’s Prime Day shopping event, which took place in the second quarter this year in most major markets, including the US.Amazon said the shift in Prime Day’s timing also affected its overall third-quarter sales growth. Excluding the calendar change, year-on-year revenue growth would have been approximately four percentage points higher, the company said.Amazon’s results come amid growing investor scrutiny of the enormous sums technology companies are committing to AI infrastructure and whether the spending will deliver adequate returns.Alphabet, the parent company of Google and YouTube, saw its shares plunge 12% on Thursday after investors reacted to its latest results and rising expenditure on property and equipment. Microsoft, meanwhile, lowered its capital expenditure outlook to $170 billion from $175 billion.The sell-off reflects concerns that the race to build data centres and deploy AI chips could strain cash flows even at some of the industry’s largest companies.Amazon is also facing scrutiny over the impact of its expanding data centre footprint on local communities. Earlier this month, the company said it would invest more than $1 billion over five years in communities where it operates data centres, including funding for education, job training, water conservation and energy-related initiatives.Despite the concerns, Amazon continues to expand its retail operations through faster deliveries, automation and AI-powered warehouse technology. Jassy has argued that these investments are strengthening the company’s competitive position, while the latest AWS results indicate that demand for its cloud infrastructure remains robust.
Article Summary: Amazon shares fell sharply in after-hours trading on Thursday (local time) as heavy artificial intelligence investments and a weaker-than-expected earnings performance overshadowed accelerating growth in its cloud computing business. The e-commerce and technology giant’s shares dropped as much as 7% after it reported third-quarter results that missed Wall Street expectations.

Article Title: 3 Wall Street firms agree to pay up to $100,000 a month to get Trump’s posts faster: How it works
Article Text:
3 trading firms agree to pay Trump’s Truth Social for faster access

How Truth API works

Who is paying for the service?

Why the paid feed has drawn criticism

Trump Media’s financial portfolio

US President Donald Trump’s paid social media service, Truth API, has found customers, with Bloomberg and two high-frequency trading firms paying for faster access to his posts. The service costs financial institutions up to $100,000 a month.Two sources with direct knowledge of the matter, cited by Reuters, said Susquehanna International Group and Jump Trading, both of which specialise in algorithmic and automated trading strategies, have also signed up for the service.The deals give subscribers a timing advantage over people who monitor Trump’s posts on the app themselves.The arrangement has raised concerns about the sale of faster access to statements by a sitting president, particularly because his posts can influence financial markets.It also comes as Trump Media and Technology Group, the company behind Truth Social, faces legal challenges over the paid service and questions about the potential use of presidential communications for commercial gain.Trump Media and Technology Group announced the faster-access product in July, pitching it to trading firms and other financial institutions. The service is designed to deliver Trump’s posts more quickly than a person could obtain them by repeatedly checking Truth Social.Trump Media officials have put the timing advantage at 50 milliseconds. For financial firms using automated trading systems, that difference can matter when a presidential statement triggers a change in asset prices.High-frequency traders rely on software to scan news headlines, company announcements and government statements for information that could move markets. Their systems can read and analyse the information before executing trades in thousandths of a second.The potential consequences of Trump’s social media posts were evident in April, when oil futures fell after he announced a ceasefire in the Iran war on Truth Social.An application programming interface, or API, acts as a digital bridge that allows one computer system to communicate with another. In this case, the product gives subscribers faster access to the president’s posts, which they can use in their trading or financial information systems.According to a Reuters report, Bloomberg, Susquehanna International Group and Jump Trading are among the organisations that have signed up for Truth API.In August, Trump Media told investors it had "signed more than 10 customer agreements”. Reuters was unable to independently confirm that figure.The company did not identify its customers but said they were primarily Wall Street trading firms paying between $60,000 and $100,000 a month. The latest deals indicate that the product has attracted both financial trading firms and a news and data provider.Reuters, which competes with Bloomberg in financial news, said in a statement: "We will assess the service, but have no current plans to subscribe."Trump Media defended the product in a statement, saying: “Truth Social offers an industry-standard API product for which there is significant demand across industries. We take customer confidentiality seriously. This reporting is based on misleading information being peddled by anonymous sources aimed at harming our company, customers and shareholders.”The company has not publicly named the subscribers in its August investor update, and the three firms named in the report declined to comment.The paid service has drawn criticism for giving subscribers faster access to a president’s statements, potentially offering financial firms an advantage when his posts move markets. The deals are likely the first time a business linked to a sitting president has sold access to his statements.In July, Democratic Senators Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts and Adam Schiff of California asked the US Securities and Exchange Commission to investigate whether the service violated securities laws. They called it a “shocking abuse” of office by a president seeking personal gain.A Trump Media and Technology Group spokesperson said, “Congressional Democrats continue to mischaracterize Truth API either out of ideological opposition to free markets or a failure to grasp the distinction between public and nonpublic information.”In August, Intercept Media and the non-profit Freedom of the Press Foundation sued Trump, seeking to stop the White House from posting official government announcements exclusively on Truth Social. The ongoing lawsuit describes the service as "profoundly corrupt" and alleges violations of the First and Fifth Amendments.The commercial arrangement has also drawn attention to the ownership of Trump Media. The president’s family trust owns 41% of the company, and Trump is the trust’s sole beneficiary.The Truth API deals come as Trump Media faces a steep decline in its stock market value.Shares of the company have fallen more than 50% so far this year. Its market value has also been volatile since it went public in March 2024.The company closed at a market value of about $8 billion on its debut in March 2024, but is now worth about $1.8 billion.Since 2024, Trump Media has lost about $1.76 billion, including non-cash charges.
Article Summary: Bloomberg, Susquehanna International Group and Jump Trading are among the organisations that have signed up for Truth API. The service is designed to deliver Trump’s posts more quickly than a person could obtain them by repeatedly checking Truth Social. For financial firms using automated trading systems, that difference can matter when a presidential statement triggers a change in asset prices.

Article Title: Oil prices rise as Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia stoke supply fears; Brent nears $116
Article Text:
Brent futures gained 86 cents, or 0.75%, to $115.74 a barrel

Peace overtures fail to ease tensions

Crude oil prices continued their upward march on Friday, with Brent crossing $115 a barrel as attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and mounting risks to shipping in the Gulf heightened fears of supply disruptions. The benchmarks were also heading for their fourth consecutive monthly rise, with US crude poised to settle above $100 for the first time since April.Brent futures gained 86 cents, or 0.75 per cent, to $115.74 a barrel by 0122 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) rose 72 cents, or 0.71 per cent, to $102.72.Brent was on course for a nearly 14 per cent gain in October, while WTI was set to jump around 15 per cent. Both were heading for their sharpest monthly increases since July.The latest escalation came on Thursday, when Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi group claimed attacks on key Saudi oil installations, including the Ras Tanura and Rabigh refineries and an Aramco facility in Abqaiq. A Saudi-led coalition separately reported intercepting a cruise missile launched towards the kingdom’s western region.The developments have heightened concerns over the security of energy infrastructure and shipping routes at a time when prospects for a diplomatic breakthrough remain uncertain.“Continued kinetic action around the Strait of Hormuz amidst doubts of a viable diplomatic pathway are keeping oil prices elevated in expectation of an escalation of the conflict in coming weeks,” said Saul Kavonic, head of energy research at MST Marquee.The Strait of Hormuz remains a major source of concern for energy markets, with any disruption to traffic through the waterway threatening to constrain global oil supplies.Efforts to reopen diplomatic channels between Washington and Tehran have yet to provide markets with reassurance.US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that Vice President JD Vance had contacted Iran to help it obtain medical supplies. This followed US media reports that Vance had written to Iran’s top security official in a bid to restart peace negotiations.Iran has received the letter but has not responded, the semi-official Tasnim news agency reported. Tehran is insisting that Washington accept its conditions, the agency said, quoting the Iranian position that “any position that contradicts this framework is unacceptable.”At sea, Iran’s Revolutionary Guards reported that three tankers had hit sea mines, exploded and caught fire while attempting to use an unauthorised route south of the Strait of Hormuz. The report added to the security concerns surrounding maritime traffic in the region.The heightened risks are also prompting changes to corporate travel plans. ExxonMobil and Chevron have cancelled plans for their executives to attend the United Arab Emirates’ biggest oil show next week, two sources familiar with the matter told Reuters.With crude prices already recording substantial monthly gains, traders are watching for signs that the conflict could further disrupt oil production or transportation. The trajectory of diplomatic efforts and the security of key energy routes are likely to remain central to market sentiment.
Article Summary: Brent futures gained 86 cents, or 0.75%, to $115.74 a barrel. US crude poised to settle above $100 for the first time since April. Attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and mounting risks to shipping in the Gulf have heightened fears of supply disruptions.

Article Title: Trent shares jump 7% after strong Q2 results, Zudio's 1,000-store milestone
Article Text:
Trent share price jumps 7%

Trent's Q2 earnings: Revenue, operating profit grow at a faster pace

Zudio, Westside expansion: Trent strengthens fashion retail presence

Star food and grocery business: Revenue grows over 20%

NEW DELHI: Trent shares jumped almost 7% on Friday after the Tata Group's retail arm reported a strong 25% year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit for the September quarter.The stock climbed 6.73% to Rs 3,059 on the BSE, while its NSE-listed shares gained 6.92% to Rs 3,060. The rally added Rs 9,088.92 crore to the company's market capitalisation, taking it to Rs 1,61,769.32 crore.The company, which operates popular retail brands such as Zudio and Westside, reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 468 crore for the quarter ended September 30. Revenue from operations rose 22% year-on-year to Rs 5,873 crore, while operating EBITDA grew at a faster pace of 37% to Rs 785 crore.Trent's operating performance improved during the September quarter, with its operating EBIT margin expanding to 11.6% from 10.5% in the corresponding period last year.For the first half of FY27, consolidated revenue increased 20% to Rs 11,628 crore, while net profit climbed 24% to Rs 986 crore. Operating EBITDA for the six-month period rose 35% to Rs 1,633 crore.On a standalone basis, the company reported a 23% rise in revenue from operations to Rs 5,788 crore.Operating EBITDA increased 37% to Rs 791 crore, while net profit grew 9% to Rs 490 crore.The difference between standalone profit growth and operating earnings growth was partly due to a higher base in the previous year. Trent's Q2 FY26 and H1 FY26 results included pre-tax profits from asset sales of Rs 96 crore and Rs 109 crore, respectively. No material corresponding gains were recorded in the current-year periods.Store expansion remained a key part of Trent's business during the quarter, with the company opening its 1,000th Zudio store. Its retail portfolio as of September 30 included 999 Zudio outlets, seven of which were in the UAE, alongside 311 Westside stores and 32 outlets under other lifestyle concepts.During Q2, Trent added 19 Zudio and 10 Westside stores, while consolidating two Zudio outlets. Its fashion retail footprint crossed 18.5 million square feet, spanning 339 cities, including three cities in the UAE.The company is scaling Zudio's value-fashion offering alongside Westside's broader lifestyle and fashion portfolio. Trent said the response to its brands in tier-two and tier-three markets had encouraged it to expand into smaller cities and hinterland locations.Categories such as beauty and personal care, innerwear and footwear also contributed to the business, accounting for more than 21% of standalone revenue.Westside's digital operations recorded 20% revenue growth in the first half of FY27. Online sales contributed more than 6% of the brand's revenue, with business coming through its own platform and its presence on Tata Neu.Trent's food and grocery business, Star, reported revenue growth of more than 20% in the September quarter, despite operating in a competitive environment.The company added one outlet during the quarter, taking Star's total store count to 87 across 13 cities. Its own-brand products accounted for more than 74% of revenue.According to the company, its private-label strategy was helping improve the business's economic profile at the store level. Tata said Trent remained confident about the food and grocery segment and would continue investing in its expansion, with a focus on building scale and strengthening its market position.Commenting on the company's performance, Noel N Tata, chairman of Trent, said, "Our brands experienced solid traction during the quarter. It was encouraging to witness a more robust consumer sentiment despite the relatively inflationary backdrop,"Reflecting on his tenure as chairman, Tata said, "As I conclude my tenure as Chairman of Trent, I could not be more delighted at the enormous strides the Company has made in recent years," adding that he believed the company's "best days lie ahead."
Article Summary: Trent shares jumped almost 7% on Friday after the Tata Group's retail arm reported a strong 25% year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit. The stock climbed 6.73% to Rs 3,059 on the BSE, while its NSE-listed shares gained 6.92% to £3,060. The rally added Rs 9,088.92 crore to the company's market capitalisation.

Article Title: AsterOne: The ERP platform helping schools go digital
Article Text:
AsterOne

One platform. Complete school management.

Empowering educators

Bringing schools and families closer

The paperless school

A platform built for every school

Disclaimer: The above is non-editorial content, and TIL does not guarantee, vouch or endorse any of it. Please take all steps necessary to ascertain that any information and content provided is correct, updated, and verified.

As schools prepare students for a digital future, many are discovering that the transformation cannot stop at the classroom door. Administration, communication and daily operations also need to evolve. This is where AsterOne, an all-in-one School ERP platform, is redefining how educational institutions function—making schools more efficient, better connected and significantly less dependent on paper.Designed as a comprehensive digital ecosystem for schools, AsterOne simplifies complex administrative processes, strengthens collaboration between educators and families, and equips institutions with intelligent tools to create smoother learning experiences. While Aster Institutions has successfully adopted AsterOne across its campuses, the platform has been built as an independent solution that can empower schools everywhere.Running a modern school involves hundreds of interconnected processes—from admissions and attendance to examinations, transport, fee collection and parent communication. When these functions operate through separate systems or paper-based workflows, they often lead to duplication, delays and unnecessary administrative effort.AsterOne brings these essential functions together on a single platform, creating a seamless digital experience for administrators, teachers, parents and students.The platform supports the complete student lifecycle with features including digital admissions, student records, attendance management, timetable scheduling, examination management, report cards, fee management, transport tracking, library management, inventory management and administrative reporting.Instead of switching between multiple tools, schools can manage everyday operations through one integrated system, improving coordination while reducing repetitive manual work.Teachers are at the heart of every successful school, yet much of their time is often consumed by administrative responsibilities.AsterOne helps shift that balance.Digital attendance, automated report cards, academic planning tools, homework management and learning resources allow educators to spend less time on paperwork and more time engaging with students. The platform's learning management capabilities also support structured academic delivery, making it easier to organise assignments, assessments and classroom communication.For school leaders, integrated dashboards and reports provide valuable operational insights that support informed decision-making without requiring extensive manual compilation.Technology works best when it removes obstacles, allowing educators to focus on teaching rather than administration.A child's education thrives when schools and families stay connected. Timely communication builds trust, encourages involvement and ensures that important information reaches parents without delay.AsterOne strengthens this connection through dedicated parent and teacher portals, app-based notifications and digital communication tools. Circulars, homework, attendance updates, academic progress and important announcements can all be shared digitally, reducing dependence on printed diaries and physical notices.This creates a more responsive communication system while making school information easier for families to access whenever they need it.One of AsterOne's most meaningful contributions goes beyond efficiency—its ability to help schools embrace a practical paperless culture.By replacing routine paper-based processes with digital alternatives, AsterOne helps schools reduce unnecessary printing without compromising functionality.Electronic records, digital notices, online fee management, digital attendance and paperless communication collectively contribute to more sustainable school operations. Every circular shared digitally, every register maintained electronically and every form completed online represents a small but meaningful step towards conserving resources.The platform aligns operational efficiency with environmental responsibility, demonstrating that digital transformation can benefit both schools and the planet.Aster Institutions serves as a practical example of how a fully integrated ERP ecosystem can support operational excellence and sustainability.By implementing AsterOne across its campuses, the institution has strengthened digital communication, streamlined administrative workflows and advanced its vision of creating a paperless school environment.The experience illustrates how thoughtful adoption of technology can simplify everyday school operations while supporting broader environmental goals. More importantly, it shows that a paperless approach is not merely about reducing paper—it is about building smarter systems that save time, improve accessibility and encourage responsible resource use.Although AsterOne has proven its capabilities through implementation within Aster Institutions, its vision extends far beyond a single education group.The platform has been developed to serve schools of different sizes, structures and operational needs, providing them with a scalable solution that adapts to their unique requirements.Whether an institution aims to improve administrative efficiency, strengthen parent engagement, simplify fee management, enhance transport visibility or begin its journey towards becoming paperless, AsterOne offers a unified platform to support that transformation.As education continues to evolve, the schools that thrive will be those that combine strong teaching with smart systems.AsterOne reflects this philosophy—bringing together technology, efficiency and sustainability in one connected ecosystem.The future of education is not simply digital.It is connected, intelligent and paperless.
Article Summary: AsterOne is an all-in-one School ERP platform built for every school. It is designed to make schools more efficient, better connected and significantly less dependent on paper. It has features including digital admissions, student records, attendance management, timetable scheduling, examination management, report cards, fee management, transport tracking, library management and administrative reporting.

Article Title: CEA: Year 2026 resembles 1991
Article Text:
Chief Economic Advisor V Anantha Nageswaran compares the year 2026 with 1991, saying India is at a critical economic inflection point (Photo: PTI).

NEW DELHI: The year 2026 resembles 1991, and it could be deemed an inflection point for the Indian economy, which has been facing not only external challenges but also structural constraints in manufacturing, energy, agriculture and technology, chief economic adviser V Anantha Nageswaran said on Thursday.Addressing the ISID-IDRA national conference, Nageswaran further said that, in the global context, India is a source of macroeconomic stability and resilience, which sometimes tend to get forgotten in the noisy world of social media narratives.“2026 resembles 1991, and many of you immediately should not think that when we talk about the word resemblance, it is not the same as identical. Identical means that you have the same balance of payments crisis.“No. The point is, it was an inflection point for us in 1991, and 2026 is also, or even 2025, could be deemed as inflection points for us,” he said. Nageswaran said that while the 1991 balance of payments crisis brought four decades of accumulated constraints to a head — a moment of reckoning more than a passing shock — the external stress of 2026 has brought India to a fork in its growth journey and invites a fundamental re-examination of strategy.“In 2026, the challenge is not only external. Structural constraints in manufacturing, energy, agriculture and technology add to the pressure,” he said.Nageswaran said govts and industries must focus on building domestic capabilities and reducing dependence on supplies that could be restricted during geopolitical tensions.“The 21st century will be marked by a geopolitical contest for real resources,” he said, adding that the key question was how much leverage a country could exercise to secure what it needs. Nageswaran pointed out that the worst shocks now arrive not because of accidents of nature, but by design. “Just as last week, we saw China announcing an export licensing regime for tunnel boring machines and for many other products of infrastructure goods, which India will be needing,” he said.
Article Summary: Chief Economic Advisor V Anantha Nageswaran compares the year 2026 with 1991. He says India is at a critical economic inflection point. The 21st century will be marked by a geopolitical contest for real resources, he said. He said govts and industries must focus on building domestic capabilities.

Article Title: IDBI Bk stake sale followed laid down process: Govt
Article Text:
NEW DELHI:

Amid protests by unions and political parties, govt on Thursday asserted that sale of its stake in IDBI Bank, as part of the “strategic restructuring”, was in line with the process provided for in the request for proposal (RFP) and the decision was taken following approval by a panel of secretaries, after approval by the cabinet committee on economic affairs.The IDBI Bank process had to be called off earlier this year as the bids were far below the reserve price and govt subsequently invited fresh bids from the two players in the fray and relied on two valuation methods before deciding to sell the stake to Fairfax Holdings.In a statement, it said the first round was in line with its internal practices, which are in the nature of indicative guidelines and not hidebound rules or regulations. “The foreword itself states that the procedure suggested is not to be construed as a rigid, legal framework, which may require due adaptation/ modification in the best interest of successful execution of the transaction in a time bound manner. Given the complex nature of strategic transactions, the indicative guidelines give flexibility to ensure cost and time spent in lengthy processes is not wasted,” it said.It also said RFP provided for ways to deal with the situation. “In the event the financial bid of the highest bidder is lower than the reserve price, Gol will decide the further course of action and the QIPs shall not subsequently question any decision taken by the Gol in this regard.” The finance ministry said the issue was referred to CoS and CCEA which “empowered CGD to remove all difficulties, including deviations from procedure, to ensure effective implementation of the strategic disinvestment transactions…”It said core group reviewed valuation methodology in April before inviting best offer bids. “The process remained double blind because the bidder did not know valuation and valuators did not see bids. Only CGD gets to see a complete picture and compares bids with fair valuations to take a final call on reasonableness of bids submitted.”
Article Summary: The IDBI Bank process had to be called off earlier this year as the bids were far below the reserve price. Govt subsequently invited fresh bids from the two players in the fray and relied on two valuation methods before deciding to sell the stake.

Article Title: September pain for credit card companies: Spending down 6% at Rs 2L cr
Article Text:
File photo: Credit cards

MUMBAI: Credit card spending fell 5.9% year-on-year to about Rs 2 lakh crore in Sept 2026, the first annual decline since Feb 2021, as festive purchases shifted to Oct and a high base amplified the fall.Spending had risen 13.3% month-on-month in Sept 2025 after GST rate cuts took effect and online festive sales began in the last week of the month. Spending in Aug and Sept combined was broadly flat, declining 0.4% year-on-year, suggesting the shift in festive sales accounted for much of Sept’s fall. CareEdge expects spending to rise to Rs 2.3-2.4 lakh crore in Oct on account of festive sales.According to an analysis of RBI data by CareEdge Ratings, growth had already slowed to 6.7% year-on-year in July and Aug from 7.9% in Q1FY27. Credit card spending rose 4.9% in H1FY27 to Rs 12.2 lakh crore, with growth slowing to 2.1% in Q2 from 7.9% in Q1, largely because of Sept’s decline.Spending fell 9.3% year-on-year at public sector banks (PSBs) and 6.2% at private sector banks (PVBs), while foreign banks recorded 9.2% growth and small finance banks 92.4%, albeit on a small base. Large issuers also attributed weaker annual growth to the shift in the festive season from Sept to Oct.The number of outstanding credit cards rose 10.5% year-on-year to 12.5 crore in Sept, the fastest growth since Nov 2024. Banks added 12.6 lakh cards during the month, against about 12 lakh in Aug. In Q2FY27, the largest private bank issued 1.4 million cards, up 19% from Q1, while SBI Card added more than 1.1 million accounts, up 18% from a year earlier.Banks remain keen to expand retail lending, with bankers reporting stronger demand for retail and personal loans and some easing in lending terms. They expect demand to remain strong in Q3FY27, supporting card issuance through the festive quarter.Spending per card fell 14.8% year-on-year to Rs 16,305 in Sept, extending its annual decline to three consecutive months as spending weakened while the card base expanded. The fall was amplified by a 12.2% month-on-month increase in spending per card in Sept 2025. Cardholders made 61 crore transactions during the month, up 23.2% year-on-year, with each card used around 4.9 times against 4.4 times a year earlier. Transactions fell 3.5% month-on-month, while daily volumes were broadly unchanged.The average transaction value fell 23.6% year-on-year to Rs 3,343, although it rose from Rs 3,201 in Aug. The decline was sharper for online payments, at 28%, than for point-of-sale (PoS) transactions, at 13%. The high base from festive purchases made online in Sept 2025 and the growing use of UPI for card payments, which generally involve smaller amounts, explain the decline. SBI Card reported UPI-linked spending of Rs 21,300 crore in Q2FY27, around a fifth of its total spending.
Article Summary: Spending in Aug and Sept combined was broadly flat, declining 0.4% year-on-year. CareEdge expects spending to rise to Rs 2.3-2.4 lakh crore in Oct on account of festive sales. Large issuers attributed weaker annual growth to the shift in the festive season from Sept to Oct.

Article Title: US trade deal will protect sensitive sectors: Piyush Goyal
Article Text:
File photo: Piyush Goyal

NEW DELHI: Commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal on Thursday said the govt will ensure that sensitive sectors, including agriculture, are protected as part of the trade deal with the US."I have the courage of conviction to announce boldly that once details are out on the US trade deal, the people of India will celebrate that not a single sensitive interest of our commerce or any stakeholder has been compromised. On the contrary, India will stand at a very strong comparative advantage, and trade is about comparative advantage," he said at an event here.The minister said that govt has so far ensured that domestic interests are protected. "I have yet to come across anybody who could find a single flaw in any of the eight free trade agreements which have been concluded and whose details are out in the market. The ninth, the US free trade deal, is sometimes sought to be politicised by a few elements. I don't know what they are criticising."Goyal said that India had walked out of Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership agreement, where China was a major player, as it would have severely impacted India's manufacturing sector.Goyal also said that despite the global uncertainty, India will exceed the $1 trillion exports target in the current financial year.

Article Title: World's largest crypto exchange Binance probes 'security breach', $6.3 billion in assets impacted
Article Text:
Suspected hack hits world's largest crypto exchange Binance (Reuters photo)

Tether, Circle freeze funds linked to incident

Binance investigates possible access through employee laptop

According to Google Trends, searches for ‘binance hacked’ surged by over 5,000% in India in the past 24 hours.

Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, is investigating a potential security breach that could have affected assets worth around $6.3 billion, the company said on Thursday. However, it has not confirmed whether funds were stolen or established the full extent of the damage.Blockchain analysis firm TRM said North Korea was behind the $6 billion crypto hack on Binance.The exchange said it was working to resolve the issue and had temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while conducting security checks and coordinating with law enforcement and industry partners.“Rest assured that user funds are completely safe,” a Binance spokesperson said in a statement, adding that its security teams were reviewing all relevant information and would provide updates through official channels once the details were verified.In a post on X, Binance said its estimated total impact stood at around $6.3 billion, with roughly $3 billion in affected assets frozen on the blockchain so far. The company added that it was working with blockchain partners to trace and freeze additional funds.Binance's initial investigation suggested that the incident may have involved a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, which allegedly allowed an attacker to access a service container and submit unauthorised withdrawal transactions.The exchange said it had found no evidence of a wallet private key leak. It added that further technical details would be released after the investigation was completed and the findings fully verified.Stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle have also frozen assets associated with the potential breach.Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said the company had frozen more than $1.5 billion in assets linked to what he described as a potential Binance exchange hack. Circle co-founder and CEO Jeremy Allaire said the company had frozen more than $800 million in associated funds in coordination with law enforcement.Binance said it was working with law enforcement agencies, token issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and other industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets.Changpeng Zhao, Binance's founder who stepped down as CEO in 2023, also described the incident as a possible hack in a post on X.“User funds are safe!” Zhao wrote, adding that although he no longer managed Binance, he expected all user funds to be fully covered as a shareholder.The incident has also coincided with pressure on cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin fell 3.2% on Thursday evening, slipping below $79,000.The suspected compromise of a DevOps engineer's laptop has emerged as a key line of inquiry. According to Binance's preliminary assessment, the attacker may have used access to a service container to initiate unauthorised withdrawals.The company has not confirmed the identity of the attacker or established whether the incident resulted in a loss of user funds. It said it would release more technical information after verifying the facts.The episode adds to persistent security concerns in the cryptocurrency industry, where exchanges and other platforms remain targets for cyberattacks and unauthorised transactions.Founded in 2017, Binance allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets and has grown into the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange. Zhao stepped down as CEO in 2023 after pleading guilty to a felony related to failures to prevent money laundering on the platform. US President Donald Trump pardoned him in 2025.
Article Summary: Search for ‘binance hacked’ surged by over 5,000% in India in the past 24 hours. Tether, Circle freeze funds linked to incident. Binance investigates possible access through employee laptop. North Korea was behind the $6 billion crypto hack on Binance.

Article Title: Trump’s DHS hit by data breach as hackers expose records of 41,000 employees
Article Text:
The officers have faced scrutiny for wearing masks and sunglasses during operations and for failing to clearly identify themselves.

DHS acknowledges potential breach

More than 41,000 employees and contractors of the US department of homeland security (DHS), including thousands of immigration and border enforcement personnel, have had their work details exposed in a major data leak amid growing protests and criticism over President Donald Trump’s immigration crackdown.The officers have faced scrutiny for wearing masks and sunglasses during operations and for failing to clearly identify themselves.The leaked information includes names, work addresses, phone numbers and job descriptions of personnel working across several agencies, including Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Customs and Border Protection (CBP), a BBC report reveals.The leaked records were published in a searchable online database called “Icepick” on Wednesday. The activist group department of peace said it accessed the information through a single sign-on service used by DHS employees, while cybersecurity researcher Maia Arson Crimew and the nonprofit Distributed Denial of Secrets helped make the data public.A DHS spokesperson said the department was “aware of a potential breach” and was working to address the situation. The spokesperson added that the agency takes security threats against its employees and officers seriously and would provide further updates when more information became available.According to the leaked data, more than 21,000 personnel listed work for CBP, while nearly 6,600 are associated with ICE. Other records reportedly cover employees of homeland security investigations, the federal protective service and the cybersecurity and infrastructure security agency.The groups behind the disclosure, however, said the database was not intended to be a comprehensive directory of all DHS employees. Rather the aim was to replace "anonymity with accountability", according to Emma Best, a co founder of DDoSecrets.
Article Summary: More than 41,000 employees and contractors of the US department of homeland security (DHS) have had their work details exposed in a major data leak. Leaked information includes names, work addresses, phone numbers and job descriptions of personnel working across several agencies. The officers have faced scrutiny for wearing masks and sunglasses during operations and for failing to clearly identify themselves.

Article Title: $6.3 billion gone, North Korea 'link': Inside the crypto heist at world's largest exchange Binance
Article Text:
Binance says it will cover all losses from the suspected hack using its SAFU fund and company money

What happened in the Binance hack ?

Hackers from North Korea?

Why are cryptocurrency exchanges vulnerable?

What happens next?

Hackers stole approximately $6.36 billion in cryptocurrency from wallets held at Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, in what investigators have described as the biggest crypto heist on record. Blockchain analysis firms have attributed the attack to North Korea's elite hacking unit, while Binance has said it will cover all losses and that user funds are safe.The attack involved the movement of funds across 10 blockchains, with most of the cryptocurrency transferred in about 20 minutes, according to US blockchain analysis firm TRM Labs. As cryptocurrency firms raced to trace and recover the stolen assets, about $3 billion had been frozen by Thursday night in the US, CNN reported.Binance CEO Richard Teng has since said the attack was more complex than initially described, adding that the exchange has found no evidence of a wallet private key leak.TRM Labs said an attacker moved approximately $6.36 billion out of Binance wallets across 10 blockchains."An attacker moved approximately $6.36 billion out of Binance wallets on ten blockchains, most of it in about 20 minutes," the firm said in a blog post.Binance's initial investigation indicated that the breach involved an engineer's laptop, which allegedly allowed an attacker to access a service container and submit unauthorised withdrawal transactions.However, Teng subsequently said the attack was not a simple case of an attacker exploiting one employee's access. "The attacker did not simply use one engineer's permissions, and this was not a single 'one-click' action," Teng said, according to Reuters, adding that it was a more "complicated attack process".Teng also said the investigation had not attributed responsibility to any individual. The exchange has found no evidence so far that a wallet private key was leaked.The exchange also said it had "temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while security checks are completed; revoked the affected address authorization; [and] engaged law enforcement and blockchain intelligence partners to trace and recover funds".Binance said it was working closely with law enforcement to ensure the matter was handled appropriately. Changpeng Zhao, Binance's co-founder and former CEO, also said he expected user funds to be fully covered by the exchange. Zhao, who stepped down as CEO in 2023 but remains its largest shareholder, said on X that the incident appeared to be a hack.TRM Labs attributed the theft to TraderTraitor, an elite North Korean hacking unit, saying its assessment was based on intelligence gathered both on and off the blockchain."TRM attributes the attack to TraderTraitor, North Korea's elite hacking unit, based on robust on and off-chain intelligence. We make this judgment with high confidence," the firm said, as quoted by Reuters.Other blockchain intelligence firms have also pointed to North Korea. Singapore-based Pangolin Intelligence said its assessment followed an analysis of transactions associated with the hack and comparisons with previous incidents involving the North Korean cyber unit."Analyzing the on-chain activity related to this hack and correlating with information gathered from previous known incidents [involving the North Korean cyber unit]" led to the attribution, an analyst with Pangolin Intelligence told CNN.Chainalysis, another cryptocurrency-tracing firm, said it was monitoring the stolen funds as they moved across multiple blockchains, including Bitcoin and Ethereum. A Chainalysis spokesperson told CNN the firm had "high confidence" North Korea was behind the attack.However, the attribution remains an assessment by private intelligence firms and has not been independently established as a confirmed finding by law enforcement.North Korean hacking groups have repeatedly been accused of stealing cryptocurrency and targeting financial institutions. Current and former US and South Korean officials have described cybercrime as a key source of revenue for the sanctions-hit country.In February 2025, North Korean hackers were blamed for an alleged $1.5 billion theft from Bybit, another major cryptocurrency exchange. That incident had set the previous record for the largest crypto heist.North Korean hackers have stolen billions of dollars from banks and cryptocurrency firms over several years, according to reports from the United Nations and private companies.A 2023 CNN investigation also highlighted efforts by South Korean intelligence officials and private cryptocurrency-tracking experts to seize about $1 million in cryptocurrency stolen by North Koreans from a victim.Unlike platforms for trading stocks, cryptocurrency exchanges often hold digital assets on behalf of their users. This can make them attractive targets for hackers seeking to steal large amounts of cryptocurrency, particularly in an industry where regulatory oversight varies.Binance was co-founded in 2017 by Canadian national Changpeng Zhao and became the world's largest cryptocurrency trading platform within a year of its launch.Zhao stepped down as CEO in 2023 after pleading guilty to violating anti-money laundering laws in the US. He was sentenced to four months in federal prison and was pardoned by President Donald Trump in October 2025.Binance has pledged to cover all losses resulting from the incident using its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and company funds."Binance will cover all losses from the SAFU fund and company funds," the exchange said, according to Reuters. Teng reiterated the commitment, saying the company was "covering every loss".In its earlier statement also, Binance said it would "cover all losses" from company funds and its emergency assets fund, adding that "user funds are safe".Meanwhile, Cryptocurrency firms are continuing to trace the stolen funds and attempt to prevent the attackers from converting or moving the assets beyond recovery.A Pangolin Intelligence analyst told CNN that the effort to track the stolen cryptocurrency was still in its early stages. "I think the cat and mouse game has barely begun yet," the analyst said, adding that North Korea was likely poised to tap a network of money-laundering organisations to cash out the stolen funds.The recovery effort will depend on how much of the cryptocurrency can be traced and frozen before it is moved through other wallets or converted into assets that are harder to recover.Bitcoin and Ether, the two most widely traded cryptocurrencies, fell following news of the Binance breach but recovered some losses. They were trading about 2 per cent to 3 per cent lower by midday Friday in Hong Kong.
Article Summary: Binance says it will cover all losses from the suspected hack using its SAFU fund and company money. About $3 billion had been frozen by Thursday night in the US, CNN reported. Binance CEO Richard Teng has since said the attack was more complex than initially described.

Article Title: Oil prices slip as peace hopes ease supply fears, Middle East tensions limit losses
Article Text:
Crude prices relax

Houthi attacks keep supply concerns alive

Conflicting signals from US-Iran peace efforts

Oil prices declined on Thursday as traders weighed the possibility of fresh diplomatic developments between the US and Iran against the risk of further supply disruptions from escalating attacks in the Middle East.Brent crude fell by $0.85, or 0.74%, to $114.50 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) dropped $0.91, or 0.89%, to $101.90. The decline pared gains made in the previous session, when Brent advanced 1.3% and WTI climbed 3%.The prospect of a diplomatic breakthrough emerged after US vice president JD Vance sent a letter to Iranian security council chief Mohsen Rezaei in an effort to restart peace negotiations, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday, citing US officials and people familiar with the matter.The possibility of further negotiations has offered some relief to oil markets, but the threat of an intensification in regional hostilities continues to weigh on the outlook for supplies. Concerns include renewed attacks by Yemen's Houthis and the possibility that the US could launch an attack on Iran after its mid-term elections on November 3.Fresh developments in the conflict involving the Houthis and Saudi Arabia added to uncertainty on Thursday.The Saudi-led coalition fighting the group said it had intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile fired towards the kingdom's eastern region early in the day, with hostilities between the two sides showing no signs of easing.The latest incident followed an attack on Aden airport on Wednesday, according to Yemeni government forces. A day earlier, the Houthis had said they struck Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery with a missile, escalating their attacks against the world's second-largest crude producer after the United States.Saudi authorities had not immediately confirmed the reported strike on the refinery, which has a capacity of 550,000 barrels per day.The continuing attacks have kept concerns over potential supply disruptions in focus even as diplomatic efforts offer the possibility of easing tensions.Efforts to find a way to end the war involving the US, Israel and Iran have produced mixed signals. An official briefed on the negotiations said Qatari mediators had presented Iran with a new draft agreement to end the conflict.However, a senior Iranian official rejected the proposals, describing them as unacceptable ideas that did not constitute an offer.Iran's foreign minister said on Wednesday that Tehran was continuing to give diplomacy a chance to succeed. The minister also flagged the possibility of completing Iran's seven-day plan in less than a week if it was adopted.The contrasting positions leave the prospects for a diplomatic resolution uncertain, while the possibility of renewed negotiations has contributed to the downward movement in crude prices.Meanwhile, US inventory data provided another factor for oil markets to follow. The US Energy Information Administration said that energy companies had withdrawn 1.9 million barrels of crude oil from storage during the week ended October 23.Gasoline inventories, however, increased by 3.9 million barrels, against analysts' expectations of a decline of 900,000 barrels.The opposing movements in crude and gasoline stockpiles added to the mixed signals facing oil markets as traders assessed the impact of diplomatic developments, regional attacks and US inventory data on prices.
Article Summary: Brent crude fell by 0.74%, to $114.50 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) dropped $0.91, or 0.89%. The decline pared gains made in the previous session, when Brent advanced 1.3% and WTI climbed 3%. The prospect of a diplomatic breakthrough emerged after US vice president JD Vance sent a letter to Iranian security council chief Mohsen Rezaei.

Article Title: US Federal Reserve keeps rates unchanged, leaves door open to further hikes
Article Text:
US Fed holds interest rates at 3.75%-4% as inflation persists, signals scope for further hikes

The US Federal Reserve held interest rates unchanged at 3.75%-4% in a 10-2 vote, as policymakers weighed persistent inflation against a resilient economy and waited for further data before deciding their next move. The decision came ahead of next week’s US midterm elections, with the central bank acknowledging that inflation remains elevated despite signs of continued economic strength.Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said economic activity was expanding at a “strong” pace, upgrading the Fed’s assessment from “solid” at its September meeting. Domestic spending remained resilient, productivity growth was strong, investment robust and job gains had kept pace with the workforce, while the unemployment rate had changed little. However, inflation continues to run above the Fed’s 2% target, leaving policymakers divided over whether monetary policy needs to tighten further.Governors Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissented from the decision, favouring a 25-basis-point rate hike. Their position reflects concerns that inflationary pressures remain persistent and that delaying further tightening could make it harder to bring price increases under control.Some economists and market participants have also suggested that another rate hike could come in December, although the Fed has not committed to a specific course.Warsh said the central bank needed more information to determine the appropriate policy stance, stressing that tackling inflation could not be tied to a fixed date or a single data point. He added that inflation expectations had moved in the right direction since the Fed’s September policy action, while financial and credit conditions had tightened for some businesses and households. However, he said he was unwilling to describe overall financial conditions as tight.Markets reacted cautiously to the decision. US stock indexes were mixed, Treasury yields edged higher and short-term interest rate futures rose, reflecting uncertainty over the path of monetary policy. The Fed’s statement leaves the possibility of further rate increases open if inflation fails to ease, even as policymakers acknowledge that employment and economic activity remain relatively strong.
Article Summary: The US Federal Reserve held interest rates unchanged at 3.75%-4% in a 10-2 vote. The decision came ahead of next week’s US midterm elections. The central bank acknowledged that inflation remains elevated despite signs of continued economic strength. Some economists and market participants have suggested that another rate hike could come in December.
